audit.title: DataLink (Push Delivery)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opener: "DataLink push-based feeds provide access to specialized data from Data Providers through direct onchain delivery." Most sections lead with a usable statement; the NOTE box gives a clean liftable interface claim.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; clean H2/H3 nesting, 0 level skips, short coherent sections, 16 bullets. No action needed beyond adding a comparison table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 8 numerals, 0 with units, no version strings, no supported networks, no update cadence/deviation thresholds. Vague quantifiers "most" and "robust" and marketing phrasing ("battle-tested") stand in for numbers.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 links, all internal, 0 external/primary. No link to the `AggregatorV3Interface` spec, Chainlink Data Feeds canonical page, or DON documentation.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Decent. The interface-compatibility note is verbatim-liftable; the lead sentence works. Term "DataLink" itself lacks a one-line "DataLink is…" definition.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Poor. 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, no `inLanguage`. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Poor. Zero snippets despite naming `AggregatorV3Interface` and web3.js/ethers.js/Web3.py — an overview can carry one minimal read call.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Middling. Covers "what is / how it works / getting started" but no troubleshooting, no FAQ, no symptom/error-phrased sections.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (DataLink, DON, AggregatorV3Interface), unambiguous prose.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured overview page for DataLink push-based feeds — the opening sentence is a solid liftable definition and the section hierarchy is textbook (11 headings, 0 level skips, no oversized sections). Its biggest GEO weakness is that it reads as a navigational hub with almost no extractable substance: 370 words, zero code blocks, zero tables, zero external/primary citations, no version or network specifics, and no page-level metadata. The honest verdict: structurally sound but too thin and under-specified to be cited or synthesized as a standalone source — generative engines will pass through it to the API reference or tutorials it links to.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics on networks, providers, and update mechanics
recommendations.issue: "Built on Chainlink's battle-tested aggregation infrastructure with robust data quality mechanisms"
recommendations.change: Replace with quantified facts: supported chains/networks, number/type of Data Providers, update trigger (deviation threshold %, heartbeat interval), decimals/return types. E.g. "Feeds update onchain when the price deviates by X% or every Y seconds (heartbeat)."
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are the highest-lift change for citation; qualitative prose like "robust"/"battle-tested" is not liftable.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal, complete Solidity read snippet
recommendations.issue: Names `AggregatorV3Interface` but shows no code (0 fenced blocks on page).
recommendations.change: Add a copy-pasteable, language-tagged Solidity block with pragma, import, and a `latestRoundData()` call returning price + timestamp; note expected return shape.
recommendations.why: Agents and engines lift runnable snippets; the canonical API (`latestRoundData`) in code defends against generic-prior substitutions.

recommendations.title: Add page-level structured metadata
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness and canonical signals raise trust/E-E-A-T and let agents parse and attribute the page.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative external/primary links
recommendations.issue: 0 external/primary links; all 5 links are internal.
recommendations.change: Link `AggregatorV3Interface` to its canonical Data Feeds reference/spec and DON/consensus to the canonical Chainlink architecture doc.
recommendations.why: Inline links to canonical sources raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table: Smart Contract vs Offchain integration
recommendations.issue: Two prose bullet lists; no side-by-side decision structure (0 tables on page).
recommendations.change: Add a table with rows for use case, language/interface, latency/cost tradeoff, and "choose when…" so an engine can extract reasons.
recommendations.why: Tables and explicit decision factors let engines build justified answers.

recommendations.title: Add a one-line canonical definition of "DataLink"
recommendations.issue: No crisp "DataLink is…" sentence distinguishing it from Data Feeds.
recommendations.change: Add: "DataLink is Chainlink's push-based delivery product for specialized data from individual Data Providers, delivered onchain via the same `AggregatorV3Interface` used by Data Feeds."
recommendations.why: A self-contained definition near first use is preferentially quoted verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased entries
recommendations.issue: No question-phrased headings or troubleshooting; no coverage of "how is DataLink different from Data Feeds?" or read errors (stale round, zero answer).
recommendations.change: Add H3s phrased as questions ("How do I read the latest DataLink value?", "Why is my feed returning a stale timestamp?") answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom and question; concept-titled prose loses that retrieval.

antiPatterns: Marketing/vague qualifiers: "battle-tested," "robust data quality mechanisms," "most recent" — replace with quantified specifics.
No dates / no freshness signal (dateModified absent) — undated content is discounted.
Snippet-free page that references code interfaces and libraries by name without showing any.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good site-level signal; ensure this URL is listed there.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are likely templated site-wide; fixing at the template level will lift many sibling pages, not just this one.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content — pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
